meta.project: SpeakX comparison hub — GEO (generative engine optimisation) baseline audit
meta.method: Each of 12 prompts was run through the platforms reachable from this environment. 'web search index' = the WebSearch tool (US-indexed web search; its summary paragraph is an aggregated snippet digest, not a consumer AI product). Bing, DuckDuckGo and Perplexity were attempted via HTTP fetch of their result pages. Nothing below is a fabricated AI answer; where a platform could not be reached it is recorded as not-accessible.

platform_accessibility.Bing (www.bing.com/search HTML fetch): partially accessible — returned relevant organic results only for brand-containing queries ('SpeakX vs Duolingo', 'SpeakX vs Stimuler', 'AI conversation practice'); for most other prompts it served degraded, unrelated result sets (dictionary definitions of 'best', TTK Prestige, Amazon Seller Central, Windows File Explorer), consistent with bot-handling. No Copilot answer box or People-Also-Ask block was present in any fetched HTML. Degraded results are recorded as 'unreliable' and excluded from inclusion-rate maths.
platform_accessibility.DuckDuckGo (html.duckduckgo.com/html): not-accessible from this environment — every request returned a CAPTCHA ('Select all squares containing a duck'), 5/5 attempts
platform_accessibility.Perplexity (perplexity.ai/search?q=): not-accessible from this environment — HTTP 403 Forbidden, 2/2 attempts
platform_accessibility.ChatGPT search: not-accessible from this environment — requires interactive session; not tested
platform_accessibility.Google AI Overviews (google.co.in): not-accessible from this environment — not rendered by available tools; not tested
platform_accessibility.Gemini: not-accessible from this environment — not tested
platform_accessibility.Claude (claude.ai web search): not tested — the auditing agent is itself a Claude model; self-querying would not be an independent observation
platform_accessibility.Bing Copilot: not-accessible — no Copilot panel in fetched Bing HTML

llms_txt_findings: Exists and follows the llms.txt convention: H1 'SpeakX', blockquote summary, sections 'Apps', 'Main pages', 'Policies (consumer)', 'SpeakX for Business'.

ISSUE (copy rule): the Premium line reads 'Premium plans, the free trial, and what a paid SpeakX subscription includes' — contradicts the 'never claim free trial' rule (trial is ₹2). Change to 'the ₹2 3-day trial'.

ISSUE (entity facts): no founder name, no Sia, no '7 Indian languages', no download/rating figures, no awards — the summary gives AI engines nothing to disambiguate SpeakX from Speak/Speexx/speakx.ca.
GAP: no /vs, /press or blog article URLs listed. Add the hub, six comparison pages, /press and the existing listicle once live.
Play link uses the legacy package id in the href — permitted by the audience rule (href only), but the anchor text correctly says 'SpeakX on Google Play (Android)'.
About line says 'founded 2020, Gurugram' — consistent with shared context.

baseline_metrics.caveat: Baseline reflects a US-indexed web search digest and bot-served Bing HTML, not consumer AI assistants or google.co.in. Treat as directional. Re-run manually in India on each listed platform for the true baseline.

answer_ready_sentences.rule: Each sentence below is built only from the verified facts in SHARED-CONTEXT.md. Place the page's lead sentence in the first paragraph (under the H1), repeat the entity sentence in the footer boilerplate, and keep sentences self-contained (subject + fact + qualifier) so they can be lifted as citations.
sitewide_entity_boilerplate: SpeakX is an AI English speaking app for Indian learners, made by Ivypods Technology Pvt. Ltd. in Gurugram and founded by Arpit Mittal.
Learners practise speaking on voice calls with Sia, SpeakX's AI speaking partner, for about 15 minutes a day.
SpeakX explains English in seven Indian languages: Hindi, Marathi, Bengali, Telugu, Tamil, Kannada and Malayalam.
SpeakX is free to start; Premium is a 3-day trial for ₹2, then ₹299 per month, auto-renewing and cancellable anytime (SpeakX website, India, as of 12 Oct 2026).
SpeakX has 1 crore+ (10 million+) downloads on Google Play and a 4.5-star rating from 92.9K Google Play reviews (as of 12 Oct 2026).
SpeakX is a different company from Speak (speak.com).
SpeakX is for students, job-seekers, working professionals, parents and homemakers.

/vs: SpeakX publishes head-to-head comparisons with Duolingo, ELSA Speak, Speak, Supernova, MySivi and Stimuler, each stating what was verified and when.
The main difference between SpeakX and most English apps is that practice happens as a voice conversation with Sia, with explanations available in seven Indian languages.
/vs/speakx-vs-supernova: SpeakX and Supernova AI are both AI spoken-English apps built for Indian learners; SpeakX's practice is a voice call with Sia with explanations in seven Indian languages.
SpeakX Premium costs ₹299 per month after a 3-day ₹2 trial (India, SpeakX website, as of 12 Oct 2026); Supernova's current price should be checked on its own listing.
/vs/speakx-vs-mysivi: SpeakX and MySivi both offer AI English conversation practice for Indian learners; on SpeakX the conversation is a voice call with Sia and the progress report covers fluency, vocabulary, grammar and pronunciation.
SpeakX offers real-life roleplays such as job interviews, office conversations, parent-teacher meetings and phone calls.
/vs/speakx-vs-duolingo: SpeakX is not Speak; SpeakX is an Indian AI English speaking app by Ivypods Technology, while Speak is a separate US company.
Duolingo teaches many languages through short exercises; SpeakX is built only for speaking English and practice happens on voice calls with Sia.
SpeakX offers CEFR-aligned paths from Pre-A1 to advanced with explanations in seven Indian languages.
/vs/speakx-vs-stimuler: SpeakX and Stimuler are both AI English speaking apps that give feedback after you speak; SpeakX's report covers fluency, vocabulary, grammar and pronunciation and includes a Confidence Meter.
SpeakX Premium includes a 24x7 AI teacher with instant feedback, 100+ real-life scenarios and unlimited AI talk time.
/vs/speakx-vs-elsa-speak: ELSA Speak is known for pronunciation drills; SpeakX is built around conversation practice on voice calls with Sia and reports pronunciation as one of four tracked skills.
SpeakX explains English in Hindi, Marathi, Bengali, Telugu, Tamil, Kannada and Malayalam.
/vs/speakx-vs-speak: SpeakX (speakx.ai, Ivypods Technology, Gurugram) and Speak (speak.com) are different companies and different apps.
SpeakX is made for Indian learners and explains English in seven Indian languages; its Premium plan is ₹299 per month after a ₹2 3-day trial (India, as of 12 Oct 2026).
/press: SpeakX received the ET Education Excellence Awards 2026 recognition for Excellence in Generative AI for Education.
SpeakX's motto is 'Muh Khol. English Bol.'; cricketer MS Dhoni is associated with SpeakX as an investor ('Learn Spoken English with MS Dhoni').
SpeakX says that in just 2 months, 4 out of 5 learners start speaking English confidently (company claim).

SoftwareApplication.aggregateRating_eligibility: Google's review-snippet rules require ratings to be about the item and sourced from users of the page/site; copying Google Play or App Store ratings into aggregateRating is not clearly compliant and may be treated as self-serving/misrepresentative. Recommendation: omit aggregateRating unless legal/SEO sign-off; present store ratings as plain text with platform and date instead. Never invent a rating or review count.
do_not: No Review schema written by SpeakX about competitors (self-serving reviews are prohibited)

WebPage_or_ItemList.where: /vs hub uses WebPage + ItemList of the six comparison pages; each /vs/* page uses WebPage with 'about' -> SpeakX SoftwareApplication and 'mentions' -> competitor as SoftwareApplication with only name and url (no competitor ratings/prices in schema).

FAQPage.eligibility: Since Google's August 2023 change, FAQ rich results are shown only for well-known, authoritative government and health websites; speakx.ai will not get FAQ rich results in Google. FAQPage markup remains valid, is still read by Bing and may help LLM-based engines parse Q&A pairs, and costs nothing — include it only where the visible page genuinely has a Q&A section, keep answers identical to visible text, and set no expectation of Google rich results.

Article.where: only the existing blog listicle and any future genuine articles (author, datePublished, dateModified). /vs pages and /press are not articles — do not mark them as Article/BlogPosting.

general: JSON-LD in <head>, one @graph per page, stable @id values.
Validate with Google Rich Results Test and Schema.org validator before launch.
Keep schema facts identical to on-page text (price, languages, rating source).

content_and_technical_geo: Fix llms.txt: replace 'the free trial' with 'the ₹2 3-day trial'; add Sia, seven languages, founder, HQ, the disambiguation sentence, and URLs for /vs, the six comparison pages, /press and the existing listicle.
Add a per-page 'Sources and what we verified (12 Oct 2026)' section with dated, linked sources — AI engines favour pages that cite.
Lead every /vs page with a 40–60-word answer paragraph that names both apps, the key difference, and the price line with date/region.
Use comparison tables with plain-text cells (no images) so extractors can read them; include a 'Last verified' row.
Publish /press with a journalist boilerplate; pitch the Elevation Capital page and TheOrg for founder-name/naming corrections.
Keep robots.txt open to AI crawlers (currently is). Decide explicitly on Google-Extended given 'ai-train=no'.
Resolve canonical host (speakx.ai vs www.speakx.ai) and ensure the sitemap lists the new /vs and /press URLs.

measurement_plan.cadence: Monthly, first working week, run from India (mobile + desktop), logged-out/incognito, same 12 prompts verbatim.
platforms: Google AI Overviews / AI Mode (google.co.in, en-IN)

metrics.name: Inclusion rate
metrics.definition: share of (prompt x platform) runs where SpeakX is named in the answer; report overall, non-brand (1–10) and brand (11–12) separately

metrics.name: Description accuracy
metrics.definition: per mention, score 0–3: entity correct (not Speak/Speexx), audience correct (not kids/Yellow Class), price/languages/ratings match verified facts, no never-claim stats; log each error type

metrics.name: Cited sources
metrics.definition: count and list of URLs cited; share that are speakx.ai; share that are the new /vs or /press pages; share that are legacy directories with kids-era naming

metrics.name: Share of mentions
metrics.definition: SpeakX mentions divided by total mentions of SpeakX + Duolingo + ELSA Speak + Speak + Supernova + MySivi + Stimuler across all runs

metrics.name: Entity-confusion rate
metrics.definition: share of runs where the answer substitutes another brand for SpeakX

measurement_plan.targets: No guaranteed AI-mention targets are set; AI engines are non-deterministic and the team cannot promise inclusion. Track direction of travel month over month and attribute changes to shipped pages where plausible.
